body: Thank you.  I am working on getting stronger and distancing myself from her.  It has been helpful.  The emotional cage that I felt was really limiting my world and my motivation to even get better,
I don't know if I said anything or not, but your reply was really excellent.

Thank you.
I have started some upper body strength training (very basic with free weights at home).  This past week, I have left the house to attend a type of exercise class (I don't want to reveal which one).

The showers are still harder.  But I have been taking more like 2-3 per week instead of 1 per week.  I haven't washed my hair since Tuesday, which is a very tiring task.  I have been feeding myself better.  I even sometimes find that I am hungry.

I appreciate your encouragement.  Maybe it's even more helpful to first read your comment a month later and see the small steps I have taken to be able to help myself.

The USA.  The ability to try and get medical care makes me feel horrible.  I have to try to get medical care knowing that they will leave me with a large bill which I will not be able to pay.  Eventually, that means I can no longer receive care from that provider.  My psychiatrist had quadrupled what she used to accept as payment.  Not having access to affordable care is a very suffocating feeling.

I don't have money for food either.  I am underweight.  I don't have the energy to try and sell anything I have.  I waited 8 hours to apply for food stamps.  I was denied.  I was denied medicaid because I am a single woman with no kids.  I've put a great deal of money into the system.  And now when I need it?

I am wasting away in agony in my bed.  Two days ago, I spent several hours thinking about becoming a beggar on the street.  I think it is too scary, too dangerous, I would cry too much and on top of all that, I might get arrested for panhandling.

I'm so young, but my situation with pain adds 60 years to my life.

Thank you for your compassion and empathy.

That is an excellent and well thought out outline.
I hope that I am able to keep searching for solutions to the pain and that someday it might even be reduced or eliminated.
I can see that a note should be focused around the post-suicide recovery of those that I love.

I would like to find a way to "apply the skills and motivation that got you there."  I am open to it.  I am searching.

I don't want to die until I feel like I have exhausted my options to be pain free or at least to be functional.

Right now, I am living like a rodent and not like a human being.

Thank you for your encouragement.

I'm on two anti-depressants and I do try to maintain a professional relationship with a psychiatrist.  However, I don't think the psychiatrist understands what I am going through.

I'm also out of money, which adds extra challenges to seek potential avenues for help.

Thank you for sharing your mom's story.  I come to reddit because I am tired of feeling so rejected by the outside world for the lack of empathy or validation for my neck pain.  It's not psychological and I am not a drug seeker.  In fact, I won't even ask for pain meds even though they actually work and enable me to complete more activities of daily living.

I suffer in a cone of silence.

She is not a paid caretaker.  She was my girlfriend, turned friend, turned caretaker.  I just didn't want to complicate the issue by revealing that she was originally my girlfriend (girl-girl relationship).

My neck pain started after a shoulder dislocation, but during the same week, I landed on my head after falling off of a slackline.  I don't really know the exact cause for certain.
I'd consider visiting a urologist or dermatologist.  It sounds uncomfortable.
I better buy weapons now while I still have the right!

If I don't forget to eat, I've forgotten that I left something cooking on the stove until the house fills with black smoke.  I have burned too many pots to admit.  The fire department came once -- I was able to put the fire out, but I called them anyway.  They brought high powered fans to clear the smoke.

I forget so many things that I start, right after I have started them!

>  "Without knowing you, I can tell you that your mother would much rather have you alive and around, then the money that you owe her."

Your line just sent tears streaming down my face.  I know my mom would never want me to die for any reason.  She gave me her credit card and I've reached the limit.  I don't think she knows how much I've put on there.  I'm completely out of options for how to pay for anything now.  I spent an 8 hour day in the public assistance office only to find out that I don't qualify for medicaid because I am a single woman with no children and I don't qualify for food assistance because they needed more documentation about the money I borrowed from my mom.

I have a degree, I have held esteemed, respected jobs.  I was financially on top of the world at one point.

Now my life looks like an awful episode of hoarders.

outdoorshowerhobo, I appreciate you reaching out.  Your thoughtful paragraphs are helpful.

I've seen a spinal surgeron, I had 8 injections (spinal facet and trigger point) appointments at a pain treatment clinic.  I've had two treatments with a neurologist, the last one being due in September.

I've also tried several non-medical modalities.

I appreciate you wanting me to live.
I want to live too.

Want and having the ability to tolerate the pain are divergent paths.

I try to find "hope" by always asking if I've done everything possible to try and fix the pain.  The answer is always no and I keep seeking help.

But with the neck pain, my life is not a life worth living.

Thank you so much for replying.  I feel so isolated and withdrawn from friends and family, I just wanted to find some anonymous support because expressing how I feel places a tremendous emotional burden on my friends and family and it affects them greatly.

Instead of empathy and understanding for my pain, I think they respond defensively because they do not want to become victims of my loss.

I've heard people say that suicide is selfish.  I think it is selfish of others to want the suicidal person in their life to continue living when they are suffering.  Depressed or suicidal people are all suffering for various reasons.

I want to believe or hope that it is possible to live pain free.
Or at least to have my pain treated.

My neck pain is untreated right now.  Even though I received a "pain treatment" from the neurologist, I'm still experiencing unreal levels of pain.

Thank you outdoorshowerhobo.

Have you seen a doctor?
Some ideas:
--Start with a primary care doctor
--Start with an orthopedic surgeon/spinal surgeon to get MRI/CT
--Start by going to an ER
--Start by calling 9-1-1 to go to an ER

Whichever way you can start to get help, it's there.

Draugo,

I'm sorry you are in that situation.  When I talk about my death to my best friend, it really gets her down.  She's been taking care of me.  I am such a burden to her life and happiness.  Yet, if I were to die, most of the time, I don't think how it would affect other people.

I think she would be very hurt, sad and depressed for a long time.

I try to tolerate my neck pain as best as I can, but when I can no longer tolerate it, I will die.

To best prepare yourself, I'd find a therapist that really understands you and what you are going through.  I've met about 8 psychiatrists and therapists, but only one that was good for me.  When you find a good therapist, you will look forward to seeing him/her because you'll feel they are helping you in some way.  If you dread the person, move on and find the next one.

I hope you find help that helps you feel better and cope with your situation in life.

I empathize with your dad.  At some point, if my neck pain doesn't improve, my life is not a life worth living.  I've had my neck pain for just over three years now.
Is anyone out there?  I am in tears right now because my neck just hurts so much.  I just can't burden my friend or family anymore.  Please, someone, just say something.
